target_customer: Warehouse and distribution operators, including Fortune 500 operations, that pay for automated inventory counting
problem: Manual cycle counting in warehouses is slow and error prone; autonomous indoor drones scan storage locations without GPS or human operators.
business_model: Robotics as a service subscription for drones and inventory data

founders.name: Jackie Wu
founders.background_notes: YC page lists her as Founder/CEO; Robotics 24/7 in 2026 says she stepped back as CEO for health reasons and stays on the board. Background not found.

founders.name: Mohammed Kabir
founders.background_notes: Named co-founder and CTO by Robotics 24/7 in 2022 and 2026; not on the YC page. Background not found.

founders.name: Jonathan Sandau
founders.background_notes: Named as founder in a Robotics 24/7 article of July 2022; background not found.

founders.name: Bryan Monti
founders.background_notes: Named as founder in a Robotics 24/7 article of July 2022; background not found.

technical_complexity.rationale: Indoor drones that fly autonomously without GPS, avoid obstacles and read inventory labels need custom hardware, perception and navigation.

defensibility.rationale: Years of deployed flight data and hardware design are hard to copy, but several rivals built similar drone inventory systems.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent was seen acquiring it; rivals such as Gather AI later bought Ware in 2023 per a Robot Report profile result.

market_need_then: Warehouse cycle counts were manual in 2018; the company found paying warehouse customers and later reported Fortune 500 customers and over 300 devices deployed.

brand_strength.rationale: Trade press covers the company but no source speaks about the brand itself; the hyphenated domain is a minor weakness.

outcome_analysis: Corvus Robotics came out of YC Summer 2018 with indoor inventory drones, spent years building hardware and customers, and only announced a 5M seed in mid 2022, an 18M round in October 2024 and a 20M round in August 2026 led by Catalyst. Hardware heavy development kept funding modest, but it is still independent and in 2026 co-founder Kabir became CEO as Wu stepped back for health reasons.
notes: Funding totals conflict. The 2022 seed was 5M bringing total to 8M, so about 3M earlier is unrecorded. The October 2024 article describes 18M as Series A and seed funding combined. The 2026 article says total raised is 38M, which equals 18M plus 20M and implies the 18M figure includes earlier money; CB Insights says 17.56M over 5 rounds. The 2026 round label is not stated, so stage is other (another outlet calls it Series A-2, unverified). No competitor sources dated near mid 2018 were found; later rivals include Verity, Gather AI, Ware and EyeSee. YC page lists Wu only; other founders come from a 2022 trade article.
